21.html:
Define Prompt Components

Choose one component to change.

  • Purpose — What your model should help users do.
  • Procedure — Steps your model should follow.
  • Constraints — Boundaries and missing information.
  • Format — Length and presentation.

22.html:
Define Purpose

Describe what your model should help users do.

  • Who will use this model?
  • Which experiment or research question will they explore?
  • What prior knowledge can you assume?
Guide a short text adventure in which players explore how a prism changes a beam of sunlight.

examples_intro: Choose a prompt and adapt its purpose, procedure, constraints, and format to your teaching or research task.

21.before:
Structure
Core Components of a System Prompt
Each system prompt is built from modular components. We’ll draft yours one piece at a time.

Context & Problem — What course, what students, what learning challenge?
Procedure — What steps should the tool follow?
Constraints — What should it refuse to do, and how should it redirect?
Tone — What register and affect should it use with your students?
Output Format — How should it structure its responses?
